target.title: fix: don't mark exact-size responses as truncated in readResponseText
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `readResponseText` unconditionally marked a response as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the body was exactly the limit with no bytes omitted. `web_fetch` then surfaced a misleading "Response body truncated" warning to users.

**Solution**: When `bytesRead` reaches `maxBytes` without prior truncation, peek one more `reader.read()` call to confirm whether EOF was reached. Only mark truncated if the next read returns data (`!done || value.byteLength > 0`). An exact-size body returns `truncated: false`.

**What changed**: `web-shared.ts`: Split the `truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes` condition into two branches — immediate break for known-truncated, peek+confirm before declaring truncation for exact-limit. `web-shared.test.ts`: Added `"treats exact-limit responses as complete, not truncated"` test.

**What did NOT change**: The `readResponseText` API contract. Web-fetch truncation warning logic. Under-limit and genuine-overflow behavior.

Fixes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` could report a false "Response body truncated after N bytes" warning when the response body was exactly N bytes. The truncation check at `web-shared.ts:275` treated `bytesRead >= maxBytes` the same as genuine overflow, without confirming whether more data existed.

## Root Cause

`readResponseText` line 275-276:
```typescript
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;  // Bug: fires even when body is exactly maxBytes
  break;
}
```

When chunks add up to exactly `maxBytes` with no overflow, `truncated` was still set to `true`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Exact-size response bodies return `truncated: false` with no reader cancellation

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm test -- src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-fetch.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
✓ treats exact-limit responses as complete, not truncated
✓ cancels and releases bounded response readers after truncation
✓ releases bounded response readers after complete reads

web-shared.test.ts  12 passed (12)
web-fetch.test.ts   14 passed (14)
TOTAL               26 passed (26)
```

The new test uses a 5-byte "hello" chunk with maxBytes=5, verifies `truncated: false`, `bytesRead: 5`, and `cancel` not called.

**Observed result after the fix**: Exact-limit bodies return `truncated: false`. Genuine overflow still returns `truncated: true` (existing tests pass). Under-limit complete reads unchanged.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end web_fetch with a real HTTP server returning exactly maxResponseBytes. The unit test covers the exact same code path.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — one additional `reader.read()` at the exact limit only
- [x] All 26 existing + new tests pass
- [x] 2 files changed, +30/-2 = net +28 lines
- [x] Under-limit and genuine-overflow behavior unchanged
- [x] No breaking API changes
